Issues.Title: Move Windows CI test jobs to the Windows 11 Helix queue
Issues.Body:
We are excited to review your PR.

So we can do the best job, please check:

- [x] There's a descriptive title that will make sense to other developers some time from now.
- [ ] There's associated issues. All PR's should have issue(s) associated - unless a trivial self-evident change such as fixing a typo. You can use the format `Fixes #nnnn` in your description to cause GitHub to automatically close the issue(s) when your PR is merged.
- [x] Your change description explains what the change does, why you chose your approach, and anything else that reviewers should know.
- [x] You have included any necessary tests in the same PR.

## Summary

Move `Windows_x64`, `Windows_x64_NetFx48`, and `Windows_x86` from `Windows.10.Amd64.Open` to `Windows.11.Amd64.Client.Open`, covering all six Debug/Release matrix jobs.

The old queue runs Windows Server 2016 despite its name. The [public Helix queue catalog](https://helix.dot.net/api/info/queues?api-version=2019-06-17) lists its estimated removal date as January 12, 2027. The replacement is an available public AMD64 queue running Windows 11 24H2.

## Fix the x86 ONNX availability false positive

The first CI run exposed a native-library collision. ONNX Runtime 1.23.2 ships Windows native binaries for x64 and ARM64, not x86. Our test attributes checked only whether a DLL named `onnxruntime` could load. On Windows 11 x86 this finds the Windows inbox `onnxruntime.dll` 1.17 and enables unsupported inference tests that the previous queue skipped.

Dump analysis confirmed the managed 1.23.2 bindings reading the newer `GetCompileApi` slot, which is absent in native 1.17. The slot resolved to an unrelated C++ destructor; calling it on a managed delegate corrupted memory and produced the later CLR failures.

- Check `Environment.Is64BitProcess` before any ONNX native-library probe, following the existing LightGBM/TensorFlow attribute pattern.
- Share this availability policy between `OnnxFact` and `OnnxTheory`, and update their skip messages.
- Use `OnnxFact` for `SelectiveExportOnnxTest`, which previously bypassed the policy through a generic native-dependency attribute.
- Add an unconditional regression test verifying architecture gating and consistent fact/theory availability. It runs in the Windows x86 jobs rather than being conditionally skipped.

This restores the existing unsupported-32-bit ONNX inference skip behavior; it does not disable the rest of the x86 test suites or ONNX export-only tests. It does not add x86 ONNX product support or a product-side loader guard.

## Unchanged

Windows Server 2022 build hosts, the existing Windows 11 ARM64 queue, Linux/macOS queues, SDK/runtime versions, native dependency versions, and target frameworks remain unchanged. The `net48` jobs use the framework installed on the Windows 11 image; they are not retargeted to `net481`.

## Validation — passed

Commit `f99805593579a2a950f3929e0ef32364c4fb45a5`:

- [MachineLearning-CI 1640570](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1640570&view=results): **all 20 jobs passed**.
- [MachineLearning-CodeCoverage 1640571](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1640571&view=results): **passed**.

| Migrated Windows 11 jobs | Debug | Release |
|---|---|---|
| x64 .NET 8 | Passed | Passed |
| x64 .NET Framework 4.8 | Passed | Passed |
| x86 .NET 8 | Passed | Passed |

All six migrated jobs were verified to execute on `windows.11.amd64.client.open`. The new `OnnxAttributesRespectProcessArchitecture` regression test executed in both x86 configurations, and the main test suites completed without errors or failures. The previously crashing ONNX Transformer assembly now restores its 26 unsupported x86 skips. Supported x64 ONNX Transformer coverage still runs: 28 expanded test cases passed with zero skips. `SelectiveExportOnnxTest` correctly skips on x86 and passes on x64.

The shared test-framework project also built locally for `net8.0`. Local full test execution was blocked by missing native build outputs; the complete Azure CI run above provides the end-to-end validation.

For comparison, the first pre-fix run [1640309](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1640309&view=results) crashed in both x86 jobs. Root-cause evidence: [x86 Release main-test crash dump](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/2a2aae02-0680-4a61-90b5-ceb92a08a09d/workitems/Microsoft.ML.Tests/files/dotnet.exe.4724.dmp?api-version=2019-06-17), [x86 Debug ONNX console](https://helix.dot.net/api/2019-06-17/jobs/36b09b76-15bb-4b74-b186-ac4d6ac324cd/workitems/Microsoft.ML.OnnxTransformerTest/console).

The PR remains a draft as requested.

Issues.Title: Preserve row order for equal DataFrame sort keys
Issues.Body:
Fixes #6443.

`DataFrame.OrderBy` can reorder rows with equal keys, so a subsequent sort loses the ordering established by a previous one. Sorting strings across multiple buffers can also throw when a buffer's next value is already present in the merge dictionary.

Use the original row index to break value ties throughout the existing introsort implementation. Reverse the internal tie order for descending output, which is filled backwards. Keep equal-value merge candidates ordered by buffer index, combine candidates sharing a value, and collect null row indices in their original order. The protected merge API remains unchanged.

Regression tests compare output row IDs with LINQ's stable ordering for primitive and string columns, both sort directions and null placements, and strings spanning multiple buffers. Additional partitioned-input cases exercise larger duplicate-key inputs. The 12 initial scenarios all failed before the fix and pass with it.

Validation on Windows:

- DataFrame test project, Release / net8.0: 1,784 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- DataFrame test project, Release / net48 and net9.0: 1,784 passed per target, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Each target was run with `dotnet test test/Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests/Microsoft.Data.Analysis.Tests.csproj -c Release -f <target> /p:TestTargetFramework=<target>`.
- Ran the required repository-root build first. It could not complete because the native C++/CMake prerequisites are unavailable; the DataFrame managed build and tests succeed.

Issues.Title: Add manual issues-only labeler workflows
Issues.Body:
Related to dotnet/machinelearning#7691.

## Summary

- Add four manual-only workflows for issue-label model training/testing, promotion, prediction, and cache retention.
- Pin labeler actions to v2.2.0 and use minimal job permissions.
- Default predictions to dry-run, one `area-*` label, and the `needs-area-label` fallback.

## Validation

Local `actionlint`, workflow configuration, stage-routing, and data-guard checks passed. No model training or live labeling was run.

## Rollout

No automatic labeling or scheduled jobs are enabled. The new manual workflows must be on `main` before runtime testing; then use staged training and dry-run prediction before enabling writes.

Issues.Title: Correct BPE pre-tokenization whitespace documentation
Issues.Body:
Adjusts the documentation added in #7716 by moving the whitespace guidance from `BpeOptions.ByteLevel` to `BpeOptions.PreTokenizer`.

Whitespace removal is not related to the `ByteLevel` setting. When no pre-tokenizer is specified, BPE uses `PreTokenizer.CreateWordOrNonWord()`, which discards whitespace with either value of `ByteLevel`. Byte-level mapping operates on the retained segments; it does not configure pre-tokenization or preserve characters excluded by the pre-tokenizer.

The remark also clarifies that each segment is encoded independently, so BPE merges cannot cross segment boundaries. To preserve whitespace during pre-tokenization, callers should select rules matching the model, such as the GPT-2 pattern where appropriate. No exception or runtime behavior change is needed.

Documentation-only change.

Closes #7715

/cc @lunosia

Issues.Title: Fix test repository root detection in git worktrees
Issues.Body:
## Problem
When tests run from a Git worktree and ML_TEST_DATADIR is not set, GetRepoRoot() walks up from the test output directory looking for a .git directory. Git worktrees instead have a .git file, so the method skips the worktree root and continues walking. If no ancestor has a .git directory, it reaches the filesystem root, where Directory.GetParent(directory) returns null, and accessing .FullName throws a NullReferenceException.

For tests using BaseTestClass, this happens during its static initialization, before the test body runs. The exception is surfaced as a TypeInitializationException, causing those tests to fail during initialization rather than execute. If an ancestor happens to contain a .git directory, the method instead selects that unrelated repository root and uses the wrong test-data paths. Normal checkouts with a .git directory and runs using the ML_TEST_DATADIR override are unaffected.

## Summary
- Recognize both .git directories and worktree .git files when locating the repository root.
- Safely return null when the filesystem root is reached without finding a repository.
- Preserve the ML_TEST_DATADIR override.

## Validation

- Exercised the compiled GetRepoRoot method against the actual worktree, synthetic regular and worktree repositories, a missing repository marker, and the environment-variable override.

Issues.Body:
## Goal

Add missing XML documentation to public APIs, including publicly accessible protected members, so that IntelliSense and generated API reference documentation cover the API surface.

## Basic inventory

A diagnostic build at commit 272f2fb0abc7ef841597da0e680992d4bfdc37fc found **6,459 distinct types/members missing XML documentation in 34 projects**, plus **238 additional undocumented members suppressed by source-level pragmas**.

## Main concentrations and examples

- **Data.Analysis:** 4,898 of its 5,153 gaps are in two T4-generated files: `PrimitiveDataFrameColumn.BinaryOperationAPIs.ExplodedColumns.cs` (3,151) and `PrimitiveDataFrameColumn.BinaryOperators.cs` (1,747). Update the corresponding `.tt` templates and regenerate their outputs rather than hand-editing generated files.
- **Source-level suppression:** another 238 distinct Data.Analysis members are missing documentation in `DataFrame.BinaryOperators.cs` and `DataFrameColumn.BinaryOperators.cs`, where `#pragma warning disable 1591` remains active. These are not included in the tables.
- **AutoML:** 227 of its 371 gaps are in source-generator output; these should be addressed in the generator.
- **Ordinary API gaps:** examples include `AutoMLExperiment`'s constructor and `SetTrainingTimeInSeconds`, `DataViewRowId.CompareTo` and `Equals(DataViewRowId)`, and the span-based `BertTokenizer.CreateTokenTypeIdsFromSequences` overload. The last example is the only gap found in Tokenizers.

## Incremental enforcement

**CS1591 could be enabled in an individual project once all of its APIs are documented**, without waiting for the entire repository to be clean.

For each completed project, remove its effective CS1591 suppression, including the suppression inherited from `src/Directory.Build.props` and any project-specific or source-level suppressions. Once clean, also remove CS1591 from its effective `WarningsNotAsErrors` so that the existing warnings-as-errors policy prevents new documentation gaps. This should be done selectively for completed projects while unfinished projects retain their suppressions.
